findings.proposed_text: Interactions and state (only when the item affects them): use the Interaction design guide; name actors, channels, incoming/outgoing events, connection lifecycle and the baseline/delta, with recovery checks (including a crash after acknowledgment before processing). For each piece of state record its owner and home, who may read it (another user's hidden data stays off their client), concurrent-change resolution, what ends and removes it, quotas, and for personal or secret data where it is shown, stored, logged, kept and removed. Choose the simplest placement (a single-user tool with no shared state runs in the client) and the lightest channel meeting the stated freshness (request/response, polling, notification, push only when seconds matter; read back after push or reconnect); cache only derived data. Simplicity never removes server-side checks on uncontrolled callers, validation and abuse limits on anonymous input, personal-data handling, or recorded async failures. For UI: record the design guidance used (identity/version or fallback), component/interaction/skin premises, truthful async feedback with a reduced-motion alternative, and default to an ambitious interactive design, naming any interaction scaled back and why. Keep it within the item; an unmet prerequisite outside scope is blocked with its supplier, not a future bullet. Put locators and short decisions in the item context and evidence_refs.

findings.block: Opening: template, explanation, start command and 'Put the original request...' line
findings.why: The section names appear in the head (18) and again as an empty template; the improve-start command appears in the head (17) and again in 'Then run:'; 'Put the original request, step result, permitted paths...' repeats what the section descriptions already assign.
findings.proposed_text: Opening file sections: 'Current context and desired improvements' = the relevant part of the original request, the step result, learnings, decisions and open concerns to assess; 'Scope' = exact candidate paths (including untracked) and exclusions; 'Authority' = approvals, declines, pending decisions and any no-commit override, each with its source; 'Environment' = runtime, commands and checks that apply. Give meaning inline and locators for detail; do not copy this packet. The four sections share about <N> bytes (Until Loop state cap 16,384; improve-start refuses a contract over 9,216); put long detail in a file and cite it. Then run the head's improve-start command: ShipLoop freezes the contract (start.json) and starts the runtime; never write the contract or start the runtime yourself.

findings.why: Four lines restate that the runtime writes the receipt and that terminal state is deleted ('Child runtime authority', 'The runtime writes every packet', 'Completion deletes the child's temporary state', 'Terminal recovery uses the retained raw packet').
findings.proposed_text: Receipt: <dir>/packet.json. The runtime writes every packet there, the terminal one before it deletes its state; never write or edit it. Recovery: if this child already started, read the receipt. active: run its next_argv once and follow the result; complete: run improve-complete without reviewing again; stopped: keep the parent incomplete, and only once the blocker is resolved or the user authorizes, record that in the opening and rerun improve-start with --restart-stopped (ShipLoop archives the old receipt and reviews). An active child with no receipt or state is incomplete; never infer completion or start a replacement. To pause, run the parent pause command and leave the child active.
findings.risk: Low; every recovery branch is kept.

findings.block: Review passes + evidence + changes (no performance rule)

findings.proposed_text: Review passes (do each yourself, on the actual files): apply this stage's review focus, fix what is warranted and commit it. Write reviews/review-<n>.md per pass naming what you opened, each command you ran with its exit code, and per focus item a finding or 'none'; put current check output in reviews/checks.md. A review text written before the pass, or a script that writes reviews and drives start/complete, is not a review. Passes are self-passes, never 'independent reviews'; a first trivial pass that changes nothing completes the loop (the runtime checks Git). improve-complete imports the last two passes (or the one) and checks.md, and refuses uncommitted review edits (pass --no-commit only when the user or repository said not to commit).

A final_result with work_items replaces the whole future queue (not append): list every still-required item in prerequisite order after reading each pending item's context; [] removes all; explain removals in the plan note. Omit work_items to keep the queue.

findings.why: Three 6-line source blocks (step-plan, run-wide strategy, test-decision) repeat files already listed under 'Results this stage builds on'.
findings.proposed_text: Annotate the builds-on list ('step-plan: steps and test_commands; test-decision: <terminal json>') and drop the three blocks.

cross_cutting: The model read only the printed head in 4 of 5 of these phases (it opened only the step-plan Improve packet). Every obligation it skipped lived only in the body: the plan.md note and evidence_refs at step-plan, the test-spec.md file at test-spec (refused once), and the whole review focus and pass rule in the Improve packets. Cuts in the body save tokens; correctness needs a few lines moved into packet_head.

Improve heads carry only the next command, opening headings and Done-when: no review focus, no 'perform and record each pass' rule, no ordered procedure. That is why a reusable improve-cycle.sh with a canned review satisfied every Improve after step-plan. Add the focus + PASS rule to the head and consider a script check (identical review text across actions, review written before improve-start).

Within-packet source lists are printed three times (Results this stage builds on / Current planning sources / Run-wide test strategy + Current item test-decision/step-plan source 6-line blocks). One annotated list saves ~0.7-1.8k per packet.

_improve_prompt repeats 'carry X locators into the child's existing contract/review notes for cold recovery' about eight times; on the inline route the contract is frozen by ShipLoop from the opening and must not be written, so the instruction is both repeated and unfollowable. One rule (cite every source in the review notes; the opening holds the frozen context) replaces it.

Stage-conditional blocks are emitted whole even when their condition is inapplicable: Backchain route and Improve-vs-Backchain restrictions in Improve packets, 'At initial plan' in State/data assessment, RED/release sentences in the closing paragraph, TEST_DECISION_HANDOFF at step-plan, the workspace-return block at inner stages, graph/join language in inline plans.
The awaiting 'answer' shape is printed twice with different fields (head without options, COMMON with options); the callback command is printed twice (head and 'Call this when done').

Producer text leaks into Improve packets (TEST_FACILITY_HANDOFF 'Planning names missing prerequisite work...'; the plan-producing references paragraph) and Improve text into producer packets ('Carry relevant locators into ... the Improve child's context/notes'; 'This producer's mandatory actual Improve loop must review ...').
